subject: Procurement: SLO telemetry access + temporary metrics exception request
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com, tom.alvarez@brightbridge.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: SLO telemetry & evidence — onboarding checklist

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — BrightBridge is moving fast on the evaluation and procurement team asked me to collect a couple of specific items so we can close the security review this week. Can you confirm the following: 

1) How does Redwood measure "uptime" for hosted inference? Is it per-region, per-model, or per-account? What aggregation window do you use for SLOs (e.g., 1m, 5m, 1h)?
2) For latency commitments, what percentile and request footprint do you measure (p50/p95/p99)? Do you isolate heavyweight workloads (long contexts, streaming) from short requests when computing latency SLOs?
3) Our procurement team needs temporary dashboard access for a 7-day evidence review. Is it possible to grant BrightBridge read-only access to the metrics dashboard scoped to our org and only for a limited retention window?
4) What artifacts can you provide as evidence (raw timeseries exports, alert histories, runbook snapshots, SOC2 excerpts)?

If you can send an evidence packet and a short note on the exception path for temporary access, I can attach it to the PO. We may need a one-off clause for limited telemetry visibility during onboarding — please flag if that's a hard no.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Principal Procurement Manager | BrightBridge

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLO telemetry & evidence — onboarding checklist

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and attached is an evidence packet that covers our last 90 days:

1) Uptime: measured per-region and per-deployment (we surface per-model per-tenant views too). SLOs are computed on 1-minute samples, rolled up to hourly and daily reporting windows for contractual statements.

2) Latency: we publish p50/p95/p99 for request-token latency. For contractual SLOs we use p95 over the rolling 30-day window for the model tier in the contract. Heavyweight workloads (long contexts, streaming, large-batch inference) are tagged and excluded from the baseline latency SLO; we maintain separate profiles and sample sets for those.

3) Short-term access: we can invite a BrightBridge org owner to a read-only dashboard with scoped visibility (model+region) and a strict 7-day TTL, after which the invite auto-revokes. For procurement evidence we also provide a timeboxed CSV export of the underlying timeseries.

4) Evidence artifacts: attached PDF (slo-evidence-packet_v3.pdf) includes summary graphs, sampling methodology, alert history snippets (redacted customer IDs), and how to validate counts. We can also provide a short runbook excerpt and SOC2 control reference on request.

Two operational notes: 
- The dashboard invite does not include raw traces or unredacted tenant IDs — exports are aggregated and scrubbed.
- If you require longer-term retention or raw-level exports for audit, we'll need an addendum.

I'll loop Neha for the invite and Laura for any contractual language that needs tightening.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
ATTACHMENTS: slo-evidence-packet_v3.pdf

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 08:09:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLO telemetry & evidence — onboarding checklist

Ben / Emily — quick legal/product clarification: when you say "p95 over rolling 30-day window" for contractual commitments, does the contract specify measurement exclusions (e.g., force majeure, scheduled maintenance, customer misconfiguration)? We should give BrightBridge the exact exclusion list so procurement can reference it in the PO.

Also Emily — can you confirm whether procurement needs a DocuSign amendment or a line in the main MSA to permit the 7-day dashboard exception? If it's just a temporary operational credential, the invite + TTL is fine; if procurement insists on contract language, I can draft a short clause to append.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLO telemetry & evidence — onboarding checklist

Emily — I can provision the read-only invite once we have the list of BrightBridge users and the scope (models/regions). Operational details below for your procurement packet: 

- Invite flow: BrightBridge sends a single org-admin email list; we issue org-scoped, read-only tokens and a dashboard link. Tokens expire after 7 days and are logged.
- Sampling windows: baseline SLOs use 1-minute ingestion buckets; we compute p95 over rolling 30 days for contractual alerts and surface daily/weekly rollups for business review.
- Alerts & runbooks: we will include the last three alert incidents relevant to SLO deviations (redacted). Those are in the attached evidence packet.
- Data export: we provide a CSV with hourly aggregates (timestamp, region, model_tier, success_rate, p50, p95, p99) for the 7-day window. No raw request payloads or tenant-level unredacted identifiers.

Next steps: Ben — please confirm the BrightBridge user list and whether procurement prefers a DocuSign amendment; Emily — if you reply with the user list I will kick off the invite (ETA same business day).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
SRE Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
ATTACHMENTS: dashboard-invite-instructions.txt
